payload.root_cause: normalize_sku() in pyshop/catalog.py is incomplete: it only does sku.strip().upper() and never removes dashes, contradicting its own docstring and the domain rule that 'dashes and surrounding whitespace are ignored'. As a result 'ab-100' normalizes to 'AB-100' while 'AB100' normalizes to 'AB100' — two different dict keys — so Catalog.get('AB100') misses and raises KeyError, and duplicate detection across dash variants is inconsistent. Compounding this, the Inventory class in pyshop/inventory.py stores and looks up stock by raw, un-normalized SKU strings (self._stock.get(sku, 0) in available(), and likewise in reserve/restock), so when a cart reserves using the catalog-normalized SKU (or any differently-formatted variant), available() returns 0 for a product that is actually in stock and reserve() raises OutOfStock. The dash-insensitive normalization defect in normalize_sku plus the missing normalization in Inventory's key handling explains both symptoms.

payload.rationale: Two defects: (1) normalize_sku() never removes dashes despite its docstring and the domain rule, so 'ab-100' -> 'AB-100' while 'AB100' -> 'AB100', producing two different dict keys and the KeyError from Catalog.get('AB100'). Adding .replace("-", "") makes normalization match the documented rule (tests/test_catalog.py expects normalize_sku('  ab-100 ') == 'AB100'). (2) Inventory keys its _stock/_reserved dicts by raw, un-normalized SKU strings, so a stock dict keyed 'ab-100' yields available('AB100') == 0 and reserve() wrongly raises OutOfStock for in-stock items. Importing normalize_sku into inventory.py and normalizing the constructor's stock keys plus every SKU-taking method (available/reserve/release/restock) makes all SKU variants collapse to the same canonical key, fixing the OutOfStock symptom. catalog.py has no dependency on inventory.py, so the new import creates no cycle. snapshot()/low_stock() iterate the already-normalized _stock dict and need no change.
